## Natural history notes

A medium-sized prominent moth characterized by mottled gray to brown forewings with pale whitish blotches, dark wavy lines, and a bark-like resting pattern that helps it blend against tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, the White-blotched Prominent is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hardwood hammocks, pine-oak woods, forest edges, parks, and wooded yards where suitable host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on oak and other hardwood foliage, helping move tree-leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
